title: Token Forge
summary: A captured JWT was signed with a weak secret. Crack it.
briefing:
During traffic analysis, a JWT bearer token was captured from a request to NebulaCorp's internal API.

The token uses HMAC-SHA256 (HS256) signing, which means the same secret key is used to both create and verify the signature. If the secret is weak enough to brute-force, anyone with the token and the secret can forge new tokens with elevated privileges.

You are given the captured token and a wordlist of commonly used signing secrets. Your task:

1. Decode the JWT header and payload (they are Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted)
2. Identify the signing algorithm
3. Try each word in the provided wordlist as the HMAC-SHA256 key
4. When you find the correct secret (the signature matches), you have cracked the token

Submit: RANGE{jwt_secret_<the_secret>_cracked}

For example, if the secret were "admin123": RANGE{jwt_secret_admin123_cracked}
objectives: Decode the JWT header and payload (Base64URL)
Brute-force the HMAC secret using the wordlist
Submit the flag with the discovered secret

hints.title: JWT structure
hints.text: A JWT has three parts separated by dots: header.payload.signature. The first two are Base64URL-encoded JSON. Decode them with: echo "<part>" | base64 -d (you may need to add padding).

hints.title: Verification script
hints.text: In Python: import hmac, hashlib, base64; sig = hmac.new(secret.encode(), (header_b64 + "." + payload_b64).encode(), hashlib.sha256).digest(); compare base64url(sig) to the third JWT segment.

artifacts.description: Wordlist of ~50 commonly used signing secrets.
